title: Managing costs: cost analysis, budgets, alerts and Azure Advisor
learningObjective: Create budgets that warn on actual and forecast spend, at the right level. Connect them to action groups. Break down cost by tag and resource group. Act on Advisor's cost tips.
foundation: Cost Management shows what you have spent, what you are likely to spend, and what is driving the cost (by service, resource group, tag and so on).
A budget is a spending target for a scope, such as a subscription or resource group. You choose when to be warned, for example at 80% of actual spend, or when the forecast says you will pass 100%.
A budget only warns. It does not stop or delete anything, unless you connect its alert to automation through an action group.
Azure Advisor is a free recommendation service. Its Cost category points out savings such as underused VMs to shut down or resize, and reservations or savings plans to buy.
engineer: Where you can put a budget: management group; subscription; resource group; billing scopes.
Budget options: filter by resource group, resource, service or tag. Reset monthly, quarterly or yearly. Set a start date and an end date.
Budget alerts: each alert is a percentage of the budget, checked against Actual cost or Forecasted cost. A budget can have up to five alerts. Send them to email addresses, or to an action group.
Action groups on budgets: only on subscription and resource group budgets. An action group can send email or SMS, or call a webhook, Logic App, Azure Function or Automation runbook.
Cost data is late: new usage usually shows up after 8 to 24 hours. So an Actual alert arrives after the money is spent. A Forecast alert warns you earlier when spending is steady.

Cost analysis: group or filter by resource group, service, location or tag. Save views. Schedule exports to a storage account. Tag reports only work if the resources themselves are tagged, or you turn on tag inheritance in Cost Management.
Other alert types: credit alerts (Azure Prepayment); department spending quota alerts (Enterprise Agreement, EA); cost anomaly alerts, for sudden unusual spend.
Advisor cost tips: resize or shut down VMs and scale sets that are hardly used; buy reservations or savings plans; delete idle resources.

Tuning the VM tip: you choose the average CPU level that counts as 'hardly used' (5, 10, 15, 20 or 100%) and how many days to look back (7 to 90). You can postpone or dismiss tips, and set Advisor alerts to hear about new ones.
Roles: Cost Management Reader to view costs. Cost Management Contributor (or Contributor) to create budgets and exports. Advisor needs at least Reader on the resources.

animation.caption: Run a month of spend against a budget, add actual and forecast alerts, connect automation, and tune Advisor.

example.title: Keeping a dev subscription under 500 USD
body: The team creates a monthly budget of 500 USD on the dev subscription. One alert fires when the forecast reaches 100% (early warning). Another fires when actual spend reaches 90%. The 90% alert calls an action group. Its Automation runbook stops (deallocates) every VM tagged environment=dev.

Advisor points out a build VM that averages 2% CPU. The team sets it to shut down automatically each night, and makes a web VM that sits under 10% CPU smaller. The forecast drops back under the budget.

prerequisites: Cost Management access at that level
An action group (and a runbook) if you want automation
permissions: Cost Management Contributor or Contributor, to create budgets
Reader on the resources, for Advisor
limits: Budgets only alert; they never stop anything
Up to five alerts per budget
Cost data is hours late, not minutes
portal: Cost Management + Billing > Cost Management > Cost analysis: choose the scope, group by Resource group or Tag, and save the view.
Cost Management > Budgets > Add: scope, filters, amount, reset period, then alert conditions (Actual/Forecasted %), recipients and action groups.
Advisor > Cost: review recommendations. Advisor > Configuration > Rules: set the VM CPU threshold and lookback period.
Cost Management > Exports: schedule daily or monthly CSV exports to a storage account.
configuration.cli:
az consumption budget create --budget-name dev-monthly --amount 500 --category cost \
  --time-grain monthly --start-date 2026-12-01 --end-date 2027-12-01
az consumption budget list -o table
az advisor recommendation list --category Cost -o table
az advisor configuration update --low-cpu-threshold 10
configuration.powershell:
New-AzConsumptionBudget -Name dev-monthly -Amount 500 -Category Cost -TimeGrain Monthly `
  -StartDate 2026-12-01 -EndDate 2027-12-01 -ContactEmail ops@contoso.com `
  -NotificationKey actual90 -NotificationThreshold 90 -NotificationEnabled
Get-AzAdvisorRecommendation -Category Cost
Set-AzAdvisorConfiguration -LowCpuThreshold 10

lab.objective: Show that budgets warn but do not enforce, compare actual and forecast alerts, and use automation and Advisor to control cost.
steps: Run the month with the defaults. Note when each alert fires relative to the spend that caused it.
Tick the automation option and run again. The month now ends under budget.
Change the Advisor CPU threshold and see which VMs get recommendations.
expected: Forecast 100% fires before Actual 80% for steady spend
Without automation the month ends over budget

validation.text: Used an action group runbook to keep spend under budget

failureScenarios: Expecting a budget to stop resources
Filtering a budget by tags that resources do not carry
lab.cost: None. Budgets, cost analysis and Advisor are free.

troubleshooting.symptom: The budget was passed, but resources are still running.
troubleshooting.fix: Add an action group with automation, or use a spending limit if your offer has one.

troubleshooting.symptom: An alert arrived a day after the cost jumped.
troubleshooting.fix: Add forecast and anomaly alerts. For real-time control, use Azure Monitor metric alerts on usage.

troubleshooting.symptom: You can't add an action group to a budget.
troubleshooting.cause: Action groups only work on subscription and resource group budgets.
troubleshooting.fix: Create the budget on a subscription or resource group, or use email.

troubleshooting.cause: Only the resource groups are tagged, or the tags were added after the usage.
troubleshooting.fix: Tag the resources (a Policy Modify rule), or turn on tag inheritance in Cost Management.

comparisons.difference: Similar alerts on actual and forecast spend. AWS Budgets can also apply actions itself (for example IAM or SCP limits). Azure uses action groups and your own automation.
Monitor alerts react to metrics and logs within minutes. Budget alerts use billing data, which is hours behind.

misconceptions.myth: Hitting 100% of a budget shuts resources down.
misconceptions.reality: No. Budgets only send alerts. To stop things, you must add automation.
No. Cost data is usually 8 to 24 hours behind.
No. You review them, then do them, postpone them or dismiss them.

architectureDecisions: Budgets at several levels: one on the management group or subscription for the big picture, and one per team on their resource group.
Use both alert types: Forecast for an early warning, Actual to confirm.
Tag everything the same way: so each team's cost can be counted. Make tags required with Policy.
Check Advisor regularly: for example every month, and watch your Advisor score.

steps.label: Budget
steps.title: A budget warns you before it is too late
body: Create a budget for a subscription or resource group with an amount and a period. Add alert conditions on actual or forecast cost, for example 80% and 100%, and send email.

callout.text: A budget only alerts. It does not stop resources or spending. To act automatically, connect an action group (for example to run an automation).

handsOn.title: Create a budget with alerts and read Advisor
handsOn.cost: Free. Budgets, cost analysis and Advisor cost nothing.
before: Signed in at portal.azure.com as Owner of a subscription (a free or pay-as-you-go account works). Work in a resource group called rg-az104-lab.

steps.do: Search 'Cost Management' > Cost analysis. Set the scope to your subscription.
steps.see: A chart of this month's cost and a forecast (it may be near zero on a new account).

steps.do: Change 'Group by' to Resource group, then to Service name.
steps.see: Costs split by group, then by service.

steps.do: Cost Management > Budgets > + Add. Name: budget-lab, reset period: Monthly, amount: 10 (in your billing currency).
steps.see: A chart showing the budget against your spending.

steps.do: Next: add alert conditions: Actual 80%, Actual 100%, and Forecasted 100%. Add your email address. Create.

steps.see: Cost recommendations, or a message that none were found for your resources.

check: budget-lab exists with three alert conditions.
cleanup: Keep the budget: it protects you during the whole course. Delete it later if you like.
